result.answer:
Here's the answer, based on this site's published rules:

**Yes, you will have to pay the ¥12,000 assessment fee again for this second claim.**

The waiver rule states:

> "Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee. The waiver is applied automatically at lodgement; no separate application is required."
> — *Claims FAQ*, "Fee waivers" section (`/claims/faq/#fee-waivers`)

This is the second incident (March, approved, and the one three weeks ago), meaning you have only **one** prior approved claim, not two. The waiver only kicks in once you have **two or more** approved claims from separate incidents in the trailing 12 months — so this current claim will still carry the standard fee.

For reference, the base fee itself is confirmed on the **Claim Fee Schedule** page:
> "The claim assessment fee is ¥12,000, payable when the claim is lodged." — `/claims/fees/`

**Silver lining:** that same fee page notes a separate refund rule — "The assessment fee is refunded in full where the final award exceeds ¥1,000,000" (`/claims/fees/`) — so if your damage assessment ends up above ¥1,000,000, you'd get the fee back regardless of the repeat-claimant question.

If this March-plus-recent pattern continues and you have a *third* approved claim within the next 12 months, that would give you two approved claims in the rolling window and the fee would be waived automatically on the next filing after that — no separate application needed.
